knowledge:
- key_parameters: chrom.remove.threshold=Threshold to remove sex chromosomes (e.g., 23 to remove Y, or keep autosomes only) ;; prop.missing=Proportion of missing values allowed for a clone before it is screened out ;; sample.quality.threshold=Quality threshold for filtering samples ;; maxChrom=Largest chromosome index to be imputed (default is 23, i.e., X) ;; model.use=Model selection criterion index (e.g., 1 for AIC/BIC/delta-BIC) ;; minDiff=Minimum difference between states to merge them ;; factor=Multiplier for sample standard deviation (e.g., factor * madGenome) to define thresholds for gains and losses
- alternatives: The documentation mentions custom freely available programs, SPOT and SPROC, for image quantification and pre-processing. Outputs of other image processing software must be combined into a single text file before importing.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for analyzing array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (aCGH) data to identify copy number variations (gains, losses, amplifications), fit HMM states, and correlate genomic alterations with clinical phenotypes (categorical, continuous, or survival outcomes).
- pitfalls: Majority of observations on chromosome Y may be missing, which can cause the imputation function (impute.lowess) to fail; hence, maxChrom should be set carefully (default 23) ;; Some HMM model fits may fail during execution, producing error/warning messages; the documentation advises users to ignore these specific warnings as they are handled during final model selection ;; Two-stage subsetting does not work for HMM slots (e.g., subsetting by both change and autosomal needs to be done in a single iteration).

workflows.name: standard_acgh_pipeline
workflows.intent: Import generic log2 ratio, clone mapping, and phenotype text files, process and filter clones, impute missing values, fit HMM states, identify genomic events, and perform downstream statistical testing and visualization.
workflows.stages: 1. Import data and create aCGH object ;; 2. Filter and process clones ;; 3. Impute missing values ;; 4. Fit HMM states ;; 5. Merge HMM states ;; 6. Compute sample standard deviations ;; 7. Identify genomic events ;; 8. Visualize profiles and HMM states ;; 9. Perform association testing ;; 10. Cluster samples
workflows.code:
library(aCGH)

datadir <- system.file(package = "aCGH")
datadir <- paste(datadir, "/examples", sep="")

clones.info <-
      read.table(file = file.path(datadir, "clones.info.ex.txt"),
                 header = T, sep = "\t", quote="", comment.char="")
log2.ratios <-
      read.table(file = file.path(datadir, "log2.ratios.ex.txt"),
                 header = T, sep = "\t", quote="", comment.char="")
pheno.type <-
      read.table(file = file.path(datadir, "pheno.type.ex.txt"),
                 header = T, sep = "\t", quote="", comment.char="")
ex.acgh <- create.aCGH(log2.ratios, clones.info, pheno.type)

ex.acgh <-
    aCGH.process(ex.acgh, chrom.remove.threshold = 23, prop.missing = .25, sample.quality.threshold = .4, unmapScreen=TRUE, dupRemove = FALSE)

log2.ratios.imputed(ex.acgh) <- impute.lowess(ex.acgh, maxChrom=24)

hmm(ex.acgh) <- ex.acgh.hmm

hmm.merged(ex.acgh) <-
   mergeHmmStates(ex.acgh, model.use = 1, minDiff = .25)

sd.samples(ex.acgh) <- computeSD.Samples(ex.acgh)

genomic.events(ex.acgh) <- find.genomic.events(ex.acgh)

plot(ex.acgh)

plotGenome(ex.acgh, samples=2, Y = FALSE)

plotHmmStates(colorectal, sample.ind = 1, chr = 1)

plotFreqStat(colorectal, all = T)

summarize.clones(colorectal)[1:10 ,]

factor <- 3
tbl <- threshold.func(log2.ratios(colorectal),
            posThres=factor*(sd.samples(colorectal)$madGenome))
rownames(tbl) <- clone.names(colorectal)
colnames(tbl) <- sample.names(colorectal)

col.fga <- fga.func(colorectal, factor=3,chrominfo=human.chrom.info.Jul03)

sex <- phenotype(colorectal)$sex
sex.na <- !is.na(sex)
index.clones.use <- which(clones.info(colorectal)$Chrom < 23)
colorectal.na <- colorectal[ index.clones.use,sex.na , keep=TRUE]
dat <- log2.ratios.imputed(colorectal.na)
resT.sex <- mt.maxT(dat, sex[sex.na], test = "t.equalvar", B = 1000)

plotFreqStat(colorectal.na, resT.sex, sex[sex.na], factor=3, titles =
             c("Female", "Male"), X = FALSE, Y = FALSE)

plotSummaryProfile(colorectal, response = sex,
                   titles = c("Female", "Male"),
                   X = FALSE, Y = FALSE, maxChrom = 22)

time <- rexp(ncol(colorectal), rate = 1 / 12)
events <- rbinom(ncol(colorectal), size = 1, prob = .5)
surv.obj <- Surv(time, 	events)
stat.coxph <-
  aCGH.test(colorectal, surv.obj, test = "coxph",
	p.adjust.method = "fdr")

age <- phenotype(colorectal)$age
age.na <- which(!is.na(age))
age <- age[age.na]
colorectal.na <- colorectal[, age.na]
stat.age <-
  aCGH.test(colorectal.na, age, test = "linear.regression",
            p.adjust.method = "fdr")

par(mfrow=c(2,1))
clusterGenome(colorectal.na, response = sex[sex.na],
		titles = c("Female", "Male"),
		byclass = FALSE, showaber = TRUE, vecchrom = c(4,8,9),
		dendPlot = FALSE, imp = FALSE)

workflows.name: read_sproc_files
workflows.intent: Read and combine multiple Sproc files along with a clone mapping file into an aCGH object.
workflows.stages: 1. Read Sproc files and mapping file ;; 2. Plot the imported batch
workflows.code:
datadir <- system.file("examples", package = "aCGH")
latest.mapping.file <-
	file.path(datadir, "human.clones.info.Jul03.txt")
ex.acgh <-
	aCGH.read.Sprocs(dir(path = datadir,pattern = "sproc",
			full.names = TRUE), latest.mapping.file,
			chrom.remove.threshold = 23)
plot(ex.acgh)
